title: Senior Manager, Fulfillment
description:
Who We Are

Chomps is America’s fastest-growing meat snack brand, redefining convenient snacking with a commitment to real ingredients and bold, satisfying flavors. Crafted from 100% grass-fed, grass-finished beef and venison, along with antibiotic-free turkey and chicken, each Chomps meat stick delivers 10+ grams of high-quality protein without sugar, hormones, soy, dairy, artificial preservatives, artificial nitrates, or MSG. Seasoned with a blend of flavorful herbs and spices, Chomps provides a nutritious protein snack for the whole family. As a minority-owned, family-operated, and B Corporation-certified business, Chomps prioritizes thoughtful sourcing and recently earned the non–ultra-processed food certification through the non-GMO project. Discover a new standard in snacking at www.chomps.com.

Traits of a Chompian

If you’ve been called nimble, resourceful, and persistent, then you might just be a Chompian. You’re a team player who’s self-motivated and action-oriented. You’re committed to delivering efficiency and accuracy, and you happen to be great at proactive cross-functional communication. You’re a critical thinker and a natural problem solver who enjoys details, research, and data. You take initiative and complete ownership of everything you do, and you’ll go the extra mile for your team, consumers, and audience. You’re hungry to learn with a passion to grow and improve every day. You also take a keen interest in health, fitness, and nutrition. Sound like you? Then we want to meat you.

What You Will Do

The Senior Manager, Fulfillment is responsible for managing day-to-day fulfillment execution and the customer service function to ensure Chomps ’ fulfillment network operates with accuracy, accountability, cost discipline, and scalability. This role translates established fulfillment priorities into clear operating routines and partner expectations across multiple distribution locations and 3PL partners. The ideal candidate brings strong fulfillment and 3PL management experience, understands order execution and customer service operations, and can turn complex operational priorities into practical processes, measurable results, and clear cross-functional communication.

Role Expectations: This role is expected to independently manage recurring fulfillment and customer service cadences, 3PL partner follow-up, KPI reporting, process controls, order exception management, and customer escalations. This role will also provide operational inputs, data analysis, customer and service insights, risk visibility, and execution support to leadership for network planning, budget development, partner governance, and material service, cost, compliance, or performance escalations.

Responsibilities

- 
Fulfillment Network Operations & 3PL Management 
- Support daily fulfillment operations across a growing multi-node distribution network, ensuring accurate order execution, capacity readiness, inventory flow, cost discipline, and consistent partner follow-through.

- Manage weekly and monthly 3PL operating cadences, including partner meetings, KPI reviews, action-item tracking, QBR content preparation, performance follow-up, corrective action tracking, SLA monitoring, root-cause analysis, and readiness checkpoints.

- Create, maintain, and continuously improve scalable SOPs, process controls, compliance requirements, and partner playbooks covering receiving, inventory control, order release, allocation, pick/pack/ship execution, exception management, and partner escalation paths, ensuring consistent execution across distribution nodes and customer channels.

- Support fulfillment budget management by preparing invoice audits, spend analysis, productivity tracking, cost-per-order or cost-per-case reporting, and cost-reduction recommendations across the partner network.

- 
Order Management & Allocation 
- Manage order allocation across wholesale, retail, eCommerce, and other channels, balancing customer requirements, inventory availability, freight efficiency, production constraints, and service commitments.

- Partner with Sales, Planning, Transportation, Finance, Customer Supply Chain, and Operations to execute customer requirements, manage order flow constraints, support inventory positioning decisions, and provide cost-to-serve inputs.

- Drive proactive exception management for constrained inventory, customer allocation decisions, backorder risk, order holds, shipment readiness, and cross-functional communication.

- 
Customer Service 
- Lead day-to-day customer service for wholesale, retail, distributor, and eCommerce accounts, serving as the operational link between Chomps ’ fulfillment network and its customers. Oversee order status and shipment inquiries, the shared Customer Service inbox, and open-order review, catching PO issues (pricing errors, MOQ shortfalls, unapproved NetSuite POs, missed ship-by dates) before shipment.

- Set the team’s structure and standards, including priorities, ownership boundaries, escalation paths, channel coverage, backup plans, a shared tracker, and an SOP library. Define and monitor KPIs such as inbox response time, on-time weekly PO updates, PO issue resolution time, OTIF, and fill rate.

- Serve as the primary supply chain point of contact for key customers, supporting business reviews and new-customer onboarding. Partner with Sales, Account Management, Planning, and Quality to resolve customer issues and deliver weekly PO status updates, cut and delay notices, post-allocation ETAs, key-account update files, and customer portal PO approvals.

- Own processes for PO revisions, cancellations, and expedites; UDRs, shortages, damages, and returns; and chargebacks, deductions, and disputes, with clear ownership from intake through resolution. Manage retailer compliance (routing guides, vendor manuals, labeling mandates, ASN accuracy, EDI readiness, and appointment scheduling) to protect OTIF and minimize penalties.

- Turn customer feedback and performance trends into process improvements, driving root-cause analysis and corrective action with 3PLs, carriers, and internal teams to reduce chargebacks, shorten PO-to-delivery cycle time, and manage cost-to-serve. Partner with Planning on retailer demand signals, In-Stock %, Weeks of Supply, and CPFR with key accounts.

- 
Technology, Reporting & KPIs 
- Support business-side execution of order management and fulfillment automation improvements, including reducing manual touches, improving order accuracy, strengthening exception workflows, supporting UAT, driving adoption, and increasing visibility across systems and 3PL partners.

- Partner with Digital Transformation, Business Analytics, Sales Operations, and 3PL technology teams on NetSuite and partner-system improvements, including requirements, EDI/API integrations, order routing logic, reporting, issue tracking, and operational controls.

- Own fulfillment scorecards and KPI reporting across service, cost, compliance, productivity, inventory flow, automation adoption, customer requirements, and partner performance, converting recurring issues into corrective action plans, partner follow-up, leadership-ready updates, and prioritized improvement recommendations.

- Build ad hoc analyses that identify service risks, cost drivers, recurring partner issues, customer compliance exposure, inventory constraints, and opportunities for process improvement.

- 
Launch Readiness 
- Manage operational readiness for fulfillment, ensuring 3PL processes, documentation flows, lot traceability, shipment readiness, customer requirements, and exception management are defined and consistently executed.

- Coordinate operational launch readiness for new customers, channels, facilities, lanes, and market launches by confirming people, processes, systems, inventory, documentation, partner capabilities, and escalation paths are aligned before go-live.

- 
People & Cross-Functional Leadership 
- Guide, coach, and develop customer service and fulfillment team members as applicable, and influence cross-functional stakeholders, by reinforcing clear ownership, operating rhythms, priorities, and expectations and building a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and disciplined follow-through.

- Partner with cross-functional teams and external partners to align on execution priorities, resolve constraints, and support fulfillment growth.

- Translate business growth priorities into practical execution plans, partner requirements, system needs, process controls, and team readiness actions.

- Provide operational insights, data-backed recommendations, implementation support, and disciplined follow-through to support leadership decisions related to network planning, transportation, contracts, budgets, partner performance, and risk response.

Who You Are

- 7+ years of progressive experience in fulfillment, distribution planning, customer supply chain, logistics, or 3PL operations, including experience managing complex multi-node distribution networks and customer-facing operational process.

- Demonstrated ability to manage 3PL partners, operational KPIs, QBRs, corrective actions, SLA follow-up, and fulfillment performance across multiple facilities or business channels.

- Experience with ERP, WMS, TMS, EDI, API, and order management systems; NetSuite experience strongly preferred.

- Proven ability to identify, design, and implement automation or process improvement opportunities that improve order accuracy, reduce manual work, accelerate cycle times, and strengthen operational visibility.

- Highly analytical and comfortable using data to make recommendations on allocation, cost-to-serve, service risk, inventory positioning, readiness gaps, and partner performance.

- Strong understanding of fulfillment and supply chain metrics, including OTIF, fill rate, order cycle time, inventory accuracy, warehouse productivity, cost-per-order or cost-per-case, 3PL SLA performance, chargeback exposure, and capacity utilization.

- Strong cross-functional leadership skills with the ability to influence Sales, Planning, Finance, Operations, Quality, Digital Transformation, and external partners without always having direct authority.

- Comfortable operating at both planning and execution levels, moving from operational readiness and issue resolution to SOP development, partner follow-up, and process improvement.

- Excellent written and verbal communicator with the ability to translate operational complexity into clear recommendations, leadership-ready updates, and partner-facing expectations.

- Entrepreneurial, proactive, and process-oriented; energized by building scalable systems, improving ways of working, and creating structure in a high-growth environment.

- Demonstrated p[eople leadership experience, including coaching, prioritization, ownership setting, and development of team members.

- Willingness to travel up to 30% to distribution centers, partner sites, customer meetings, and cross-functional business reviews.

title: Senior Customer Integration Engineer
description:
Job Title: Senior Customer Integration Engineer 

Department: Product Delivery 

About the Role : The Senior Customer Integration Engineer combines hands-on integration engineering with customer-facing technical leadership in multi-organization healthcare environments, working with state agencies, HIEs, EHR vendors, and implementation partners to determine how systems interact and exchange data. The position supports integration delivery across customer projects, including enterprise initiatives involving multiple systems, organizations, and technical stakeholders. The engineer is expected to understand how individual integrations fit within broader customer initiatives, identify technical dependencies, and provide technical guidance. For designated customers, the role may involve sustained technical engagement across multiple initiatives while continuing to support other integration projects.

What You'll Do :

- Apply systems thinking to understand how applications, data flows, and technical dependencies interact across customer environments, and recommend feasible integration approaches using existing platform capabilities and standards.

- Configure, implement, test, and troubleshoot healthcare integrations involving REST APIs, FHIR, authentication protocols, database-backed configurations, and secure data exchange.

- Provide ongoing technical consultation for designated customers, maintaining continuity across integration initiatives and evolving requirements.

- Lead and participate in technical discussions with customer IT teams, enterprise architects, technology vendors, and implementation partners to understand the broader technical environment and guide integration decisions.

- Analyze internal and external technical specifications, API documentation, FHIR Implementation Guides, payloads, and application logs to validate integration approaches and resolve issues.

- Collaborate with Product, Engineering, and implementation teams to investigate technical issues, address integration requirements, and identify product dependencies.

- Develop and maintain technical documentation, including integration configurations, data flows, and implementation decisions.

- Develop scripts, reusable utilities, and automation to improve integration testing, troubleshooting, and delivery efficiency.

You’re a great fit for this role if :

- 5+ years of experience in healthcare integration engineering, interoperability, systems integration, or related technical implementation roles.

- Hands-on experience configuring, implementing, testing, and troubleshooting healthcare integrations, rather than solely designing solutions or coordinating technical teams.

- Experience independently leading or actively contributing to technical discussions with customer IT teams, architects, vendors, and implementation partners to evaluate integration approaches, identify dependencies, and explain technical options and limitations.

- Practical experience implementing and troubleshooting integrations involving REST APIs, HL7v2, FHIR, or similar healthcare data exchange technologies.

- Experience using SQL and relational databases for integration configuration and troubleshooting.

- Hands-on experience with FHIR R4, US Core, FHIR Implementation Guides, REST APIs.

- Experience with EHR integrations, Python or JavaScript scripting, cloud technologies, and multi-organization interoperability initiatives is preferred.

- Strong systems thinking, including the ability to understand a customer's broader technical environment, recognize how individual integrations fit together, and recommend feasible implementation approaches.

- Experience working with AWS services or similar cloud technologies to configure and troubleshoot integrations

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent education and experience.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Data Pipeline
description:
Bloomreach is building the world’s premier agentic platform for personalization .We’re revolutionizing how businesses connect with their customers, building and deploying AI agents to personalize the entire customer journey.

- We're taking autonomous search mainstream, making product discovery more intuitive and conversational for customers, and more profitable for businesses.

- We’re making conversational shopping a reality, connecting every shopper with tailored guidance and product expertise — available on demand, at every touchpoint in their journey.

- We're designing the future of autonomous marketing , taking the work out of workflows, and reclaiming the creative, strategic, and customer-first work marketers were always meant to do.

And we're building all of that on the intelligence of a single AI engine — Loomi — so that personalization isn't only autonomous…it's also consistent.From retail to financial services, hospitality to gaming, businesses use Bloomreach to drive higher growth and lasting loyalty. We power personalization for more than 1,400 global brands, including American Eagle, Sonepar, and Pandora.

We want you to join us full-time as a Senior Software Engineer in our Data Pipeline team. We work remotely first (from Central & Eastern Europe) , but we are more than happy to meet you in our nice offices in Bratislava, Brno or Prague . And if you are interested in who will be your engineering manager, check out Adam's LinkedIn . Intrigued? Read on 🙂…

Your responsibilities

- You will develop a data pipeline processing a large amount of data reliably and at a high rate using Python, Go, MongoDB, GCP and much more.

- For example, our clients feed their visitors’ behavior through real-time tracking to our platform. The data then can be analyzed and used for marketing automation. We process tens of thousands of requests per second 🚀. You may help improve the efficiency of our workers, improve monitoring or help with autoscaling of our infrastructure.

- Imports are critical for our clients to utilize our platform to the fullest. You may help us to improve the throughput and reliability of our imports as we need to import millions of rows of data or help us implement integration with another data storage.

- We also are responsible for exporting data from our platform to Google’s BigQuery using google’s DataFlows, PySpark and Apache Beam allowing data access by our clients

- You will help us run and support our services in production handling high-volume traffic using Google Cloud Platform and Kubernetes .

- You will review the code of your peers and they'll review yours. We have high code quality standards and the four-eyes principle is a must!

- You will start on easier, self-contained projects and once you feel at home, you can move to real beasts. Challenging, complex projects that will leave a mark - we have plenty of those 💪.

- Later you might help us by participating in on-call rotation keeping our services up and running 🚀.

Your qualifications

- You have experience with Python and a solid grasp of engineering practices 🔧.

- If you have an experience with Go , that's a big advantage 💪.

- You have experience with ETL pipelines, ingest on a scale, starting from various connectors to SQL and non-SQL sources, followed by data cleanup, sanitization and transformations resulting in loading cleaned-up data into optimise storages for a given use-case

- You know how to behave in a remote-first environment 

- You are able to learn and adapt . It'll be handy while exploring new tech, navigating our not-so-small code base, or when iterating on our team processes.

Our tech stack

- Python, GO

- Apache Kafka, Kubernetes, GitLab

- Google Cloud Platform, DataFlow, PySpark, Apache Beam, BigQuery, BigLake Table

- DataProc, PySpark, Flink, 

- Mongo, Redis

- … and much more 🙂

Your success story

- During the first 30 days, you will get to know the team, the company, and the most important processes. You’ll work on your first tasks . We will help you to get familiar with our codebase and our product .

- During the first 90 days, you will participate in your first, more complex projects . You will help the team to find solutions to various problems , break the solution down into smaller tasks and participate in implementation. You will learn how we identify problems, how we prioritize our efforts, and how we deliver value to our customers .

- During the first 180 days, you’ll become an integral part of the team. You will achieve the first goals we will set together to help you grow and explore new and interesting things. You will help us to deliver multi-milestone projects bringing great value to our customers. You will help us mitigate your first incidents and eventually even join the on-call rotation. You will get a sense of where the team is heading and you’ll help us to shape our future .

- Finally, you’ll find out that our values are truly lived by us 💛. We are dreamers and builders . Join us!

title: Data Scientist
description:
Why Faculty? 

We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here .

We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.

Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

About the Team 

Our Energy, Transition and Environment business unit is pioneering meaningful change in the clean energy revolution. Our vision is to accelerate the transition to net-zero emissions and drive efficiencies for a new era of utility companies.

We believe that the responsible, and intelligent, deployment of AI is critical to the success of this mission. We partner with a wide range of clients - from major energy operators, to GreenTech startups, and national infrastructure providers - to build solutions which return measurable impact and move us towards a smarter, cleaner, and more sustainable world.

About the role: 

As a Data Scientist II at Faculty, you will lead the design of end-to-end analytical approaches, developing high-quality models that solve complex, multi-faceted business problems. Joining our Applied AI division, you will leverage advanced programming to turn high-level client needs into rigorous mathematical frameworks. 

This role is for an ambitious practitioner ready to own the delivery of robust, scalable model components while ensuring every solution is mathematically sound and ethically responsible. You will play a vital part in pushing our technical boundaries and mentoring others.

What you'll be doing: 

- Designing and implementing core data science approaches for project workstreams, including the selection of optimal algorithms and validation strategies.

- Combining deep domain expertise with advanced machine learning techniques to solve unique and complex business challenges.

- Owning the end-to-end delivery of specific model components, ensuring they are scalable, robust, and mathematically precise.

- Developing innovative algorithms or adapting existing frameworks to meet bespoke client requirements and technical constraints.

- Building the software architecture required to wrap models and agentic workflows into production-grade, reliable environments.

- Supporting Level 1 Data Scientists by providing technical guidance and conducting rigorous peer reviews on modeling tasks.

- Managing personal delivery timelines while proactively identifying and mitigating technical risks or data limitations within projects.

Who we're looking for: 

- You possess expertise in statistical modeling and deep learning frameworks, such as PyTorch or TensorFlow, to implement complex paradigms.

- You are disciplined in extracting valid insights from messy or incomplete datasets, ensuring solutions remain robust under uncertainty.

- You have the ability to translate high-level, ambiguous client needs into actionable data science requirements and mathematical frameworks.

- You promote a culture of shared best practices, ensuring all AI development is transparent, ethical, and held to high peer-reviewed standards.

- You are a clear communicator who can manage technical discussions with customers and articulate project feasibility and delivery timelines.

- You are highly proficient in advanced Python and harness frameworks, capable of building the architectures necessary for production-grade AI.

Our Interview Process 

- Talent Team Screen (30 minutes)

- Take Home Technical Assessment

- Technical Interview (90 minutes)

- Commercial Interview (60 minutes)

Our Recruitment Ethos 

We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.

If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours. 

A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.

The Machine Learning Platform team builds the software foundations that enable data scientists and machine learning engineers to develop, validate, deploy, and operate models safely and efficiently in production. In this role, you’ll lead complex platform work from business context through production outcomes, combining hands-on engineering, architectural judgment, production ownership, and mentorship. In your first year, success means leading meaningful platform initiatives, improving reliability and developer experience, and becoming a trusted technical leader for the ML platform. 

At Oportun, we move fast and hold each other to a high bar. You’ll partner across Data Science, Product, Risk, Fraud, and Engineering to solve ambiguous problems and move the needle for members and the business.

The right fit looks like this 

You do not need detailed implementation direction to be effective. Given an ambiguous problem and sufficient context, you can define the technical approach, explain trade-offs, align stakeholders, lead delivery, and own the outcome after launch. 

You’re comfortable navigating complexity and don’t wait for perfect information to move forward. You communicate clearly, give direct feedback, mentor others, and connect engineering work to member, business, and operational outcomes.

- Familiarity with monitoring model quality, data quality, feature coverage, latency, reliability, or cost efficiency, and experience working with sensitive data in a regulated or financial-services environment.

We b uild with AI. We lead with judgment. 

AI isn't a feature here. It's how we work. 

We're excited about what AI makes possible, and we're looking for people who share that curiosity. You don't need to be an expert. You need to be open to experimenting , willing to learn, and able to apply new tools in ways that actually move the needle.

title: Staff Product Designer
description:
Superhuman offers a dynamic hybrid working model for this role. This flexible approach gives team members the best of both worlds: plenty of focus time along with in-person collaboration that helps foster trust, innovation, and a strong team culture. 

About Superhuman

Superhuman is an AI productivity suite that makes AI work for everyone. Over 40 million people rely on it daily to get work done. A recognized leader in productivity tools, Superhuman is the maker of popular products including Docs, Fathom, Go, GPTZero, Grammarly, and Mail. The newest product, Superhuman Go, builds on Grammarly’s ability to deliver help everywhere people work. It lets anyone build proactive agents that act as teammates across more than 1 million apps and websites, without changing how they work. Learn more at superhuman.com .

The Opportunity

At Superhuman, we're on a mission to redefine how people communicate and get work done with AI. We're hiring an experienced Staff Product Designer to join the Agents team in Berlin.

We're designing entirely new interaction patterns around how AI and humans work together through agents, through writing, from fixing your grammar to helping you schedule meetings. We're looking for someone to help us on that journey, help us build out new agents across Grammarly and Superhuman Go, and really define what these modern interaction patterns will be. You'd be involved end to end, partnering closely with our engineering and product teams, from Kyiv to Silicon Valley.

In This Role You Will:

- Design zero to one agents. New writing and communication agents, built as AI-first products. A lot of the job is inventing interaction patterns that don't exist yet rather than applying ones that do.

- Work with designers you'll learn from. The team spans San Francisco and Europe, with people who've come from some of the best product companies around. If you're looking for a design-focused environment with a lot of people to learn from, you'll get that here.

- Pioneer new AI design workflows. The way we design is changing underneath us. We often start in code, refine in Figma, and ship frontend changes back into the codebase. We're defining that way of working as we go, and we want people who are excited to help build something that lets designers make whatever they can imagine.

- Shape design strategy. Bring user insights, prototype ideas, and help build a longer-term view of where the Agents roadmap goes.

- Lead and mentor. Raise the standard through critique, feedback, and working closely with less experienced designers.

Qualifications

- Proficiency in industry-standard tools such as Figma and Claude Design is expected. The following outlines the skills and experience that will set exceptional candidates apart for this role.

- Extensive experience designing complex, scalable software. The kind of tool people sit inside all day, so productivity tools, creative or CAD software, developer tools. Most of that depth lives on desktop, so mobile isn't a primary focus for this role.

- A genuine interest in AI technology, both conceptually and in practical workflows like reading, writing and translating, and you're already experimenting with AI-driven prototyping.

- You care about language and writing. Words are the product here, so we want someone who also thinks about how a sentence works, what makes writing sound like a person, and how tone shifts depending on who you're talking to, not just the interface around the words.

- Comfortable working with metrics and data-driven design decision-making.

- Bonus is having worked directly in code and shipped PRs to production.

Compensation and Benefits

- Professional growth: We believe that autonomy and trust are key to empowering our team members to do their best, most innovative work in a way that aligns with their interests, talents, and well-being. We also support professional development and advancement with training, coaching, and regular feedback.

- A connected team: Superhuman builds a product that helps people connect, and we apply this mindset to our own team. Our remote-first hybrid model enables a highly collaborative culture. We work to foster belonging among team members in a variety of ways. This includes our employee resource groups, Superhuman Circles, which promote connection among those with shared identities including BIPOC and LGBTQIA+ team members, women, and parents. We also celebrate our colleagues and accomplishments with global, local, and team-specific programs.

- Comprehensive benefits for candidates based in Germany: Superhuman offers all team members competitive pay along with a benefits package encompassing life care (including mental health care and risk benefits) and ample and defined time off. We also offer support to set up a home office, wellness and pet care stipends, learning and development opportunities, and more.

- Relocation Support: Superhuman provides comprehensive relocation support to make your move to Berlin seamless. Our package includes visa assistance, destination services to help you and your family settle in comfortably, and a relocation bonus to cover additional expenses, such as temporary housing.

We encourage you to apply

At Superhuman, we value our differences, and we encourage all to apply. Superhuman is an equal-opportunity company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race or ethnic origin, religion or belief, gender, disability, sexual identity, or age.

- Main use cases moving from ‘win’ to production

- Enablement / user growth plan

- Product adoption (strategy and activities to increase adoption of Databricks’ Lakehouse vision)

What we look for:

You'll join the Security Engineering Team and will be the Senior Security Architect for Ledger's products, the cloud they run on and the partners built into them, from our consumer apps and services to our enterprise custody platform. title: Senior Applied AI Scientist, Commerce Foundation Models
description:
Who We Are 

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

About the team 

Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, e-commerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people.

About the role 

We’re looking for experienced applied scientists in two tracks: pre-training, and post-training and continual learning. Each scientist will own a focused research direction within a track. The areas below describe the team’s research agenda; we are looking for depth in one or more of them.

The role involves designing experiments, writing the code to run them, analysing results and developing training methods that other teams can use. Scientists own the research questions, training objectives and evidence needed to decide whether a change works, and work with ML engineers to turn successful experiments into reliable training runs. We are a team of around 30 engineers with a flat structure, working directly with portfolio companies to define problems, evaluate models and bring successful work into production.

In the first three months, the expectation is to establish strong baselines in a chosen research area, develop and evaluate an improvement, and work with the relevant teams to test it in a downstream application.

Track 1: Pre-training 

This track focuses on continued pre-training of open-weight models on commerce data, including how we represent that data, allocate training compute and transfer capabilities to smaller models. Research areas include:

- Studying scaling behaviour, data mixtures and compute allocation to decide what goes into the next training run.

- Developing mid-training methods, including data refinement, annealing schedules, context extension and alignment between text and semantic IDs for users, items and merchants.

- Designing training sequences from user histories, merchant catalogues and market data, and studying how representations transfer across companies, languages and commerce categories.

- Building synthetic data pipelines and measuring their contribution through controlled comparisons with real data.

- Distilling the base model into smaller models, including through on-policy distillation, and measuring the trade-offs between quality, inference cost and latency.

- Developing evaluations that help select pre-training runs and predict downstream performance, including checks for temporal leakage, generalisation to new users and items, and retention of existing capabilities.

- Tabular foundation models are a possible specialisation: pre-training and in-context learning on structured commerce data, using synthetic and real tables and comparing results with established tabular methods.

Relevant experience includes continued pre-training or mid-training, data mixture research, scaling laws, tokenisation, entity representations, distillation, or tabular foundation models such as TabPFN and TabICL.

Track 2: Post-training and continual learning 

This track focuses on adapting LCM to commerce tasks and learning from interactions after deployment. The goal is to turn signals from a continuous stream of billions of user sessions across the portfolio into regular updates to model weights, while retaining the capabilities the model has already learned. Research areas include:

- Developing post-training methods using supervised fine-tuning, preference optimisation such as DPO, and reinforcement learning with verifiable or learned rewards, including GRPO and PPO.

- Learning from session histories, searches, clicks, purchases, repeat orders and operator feedback. This includes data selection, credit assignment and reward design that account for exposure bias, delayed outcomes and the difference between observed engagement and incremental business value.

- Studying how to combine new interactions with historical data, how frequently to update models, when an update is ready for deployment, and how to preserve performance as user behaviour and catalogues change.

- Building RL environments with simulated users, catalogues and multi-step commerce tasks, including inspecting trajectories, validating rewards and testing whether improvements in simulation transfer to real interactions.

- Developing reward models and LLM-based graders, calibrating them against expert judgments and observed outcomes, and testing for reward hacking, sycophancy and excessive concentration on popular items.

- Training decision models for rankings, offers and promotions using contextual bandits or offline RL, with off-policy evaluation to estimate value and uncertainty, identify gaps in the available evidence and inform controlled online experiments.

- Developing automated experiments that propose and test changes to training methods, prompts, tools or agent control flow, evaluated on held-out tasks and regression tests before acceptance.

Relevant experience includes language-model post-training, reinforcement learning, reward modelling, agent training environments, continual learning, or offline RL and bandits applied to real decisions. The training experience required will depend on the research direction.

Responsibilities across both tracks 

- Define success with portfolio teams and evaluate models against strong baselines, including existing production systems, accounting for inference cost, latency and the business outcome the model is meant to improve.

- Design reproducible experiments with appropriate ablations, uncertainty estimates and failure analysis, using future-period and held-out evaluations, and test whether offline improvements hold online.

- Work with data and engineering teams on provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy-aware handling of customer histories.

- Publish research and contribute models, benchmarks, environments and training methods to open source where the work and data can be shared.

- Mentor colleagues, review experiment designs and communicate findings clearly enough to support training and deployment decisions.

Minimum qualifications 

- A PhD or equivalent industry research experience in machine learning, computer science, statistics or a related field.

- At least five years of research or applied science experience in machine learning, including doctoral research, with hands-on experience designing and running model-training experiments. For Track 1, this should include pre-training or mid-training of language models. For Track 2, it should include language-model post-training, or reinforcement learning and decision-model training relevant to the specialisation.

- Evidence of original research through papers, released models, public benchmarks, open-source projects or significant research contributions to deployed systems.

- Strong Python and PyTorch skills, with experience implementing experiments and debugging training runs in a shared research codebase. Work on large language models requires hands-on experience with distributed training.

- Sound experimental judgment, including strong baselines, statistical analysis and the willingness to report negative results.

- Clear written and verbal communication.

Preferred qualifications 

- Experience implementing and debugging training methods in frameworks such as Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, NeMo RL, verl or OpenRLHF, depending on the chosen track.

- Research in recommender systems, generative retrieval, semantic IDs or user behaviour modelling.

- Experience with synthetic data, model distillation or compression for production.

- Experience working with marketplace or commerce data and evaluating changes through online experiments.

What we offer 

- Autonomy to design experiments and make technical decisions within your research direction.

- Proprietary commerce data, B300 and H200 GPUs for large-scale training, and external models for evaluation and benchmarking.

- The opportunity to take research from early experiments through publication and deployment, working directly with portfolio teams on products used by millions of people.

- Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems.

- An uncapped budget to recruit and mentor research interns for your projects, with access to candidates through our connections with leading universities.

- Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants.

- A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role.

- Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro.

How to apply 

If you want to work on these problems, we would like to hear from you. Please indicate the track and research areas that best match your experience, and include examples of work that show your contribution.

Why Prosus? 

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.

Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing. 

Curious about our perks and benefits? Take a look at this page . 

Our Diversity & Inclusion Commitment 

We respect the dignity and human rights of individuals and communities wherever we operate in the world. Building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome and can thrive is critical for us. We provide access to education, which helps everyone understand the important role they play and the positive impact they can have.

title: Director, GTM AI Engineering
description:
Who we are 

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role: 

Samsara’s Machine Learning, AI, Analytics & Data (MAAD) team builds the intelligence and technology that helps our go-to-market teams work faster, make better decisions, and spend more time with customers.

As the Director, GTM AI Engineering you’ll run our AI Engineering team for GTM. You’ll work closely with Data Science, Analytics, and Data Engineering to serve Sales, Customer Success, Support, Enablement, and GTM leadership. This is a hands-on Director role. Expect to spend about 70% of your time building (prototyping agents, writing code, designing evals) and about 30% leading the team, setting strategy, and influencing stakeholders.

You’ll build intelligent workflow experiences. That ranges from AI agents and copilots that take manual work off sellers’ plates, to signals for propensity and prioritization, to the data, evaluation, and measurement foundations that make these products reliable and trusted.

The ideal candidate is AI-native. You already run your own work through agents every day, you’ve shipped AI products to production, and you get as excited about a seller’s first “wow, this saved me an hour” moment as you do about a clean architecture.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US.

In this role, you will: 

- Build hands-on. Prototype, ship, and iterate on AI agents, copilots, and workflow automations for GTM teams, from the first demo to a production system people rely on.

- Build the platform, not just the apps. Own the architecture of the shared GTM AI platform: orchestration, LLM and tool gateways, identity and access, and the MCP and SDK contracts that let the GTM web app, Salesforce, Slack, desktop, and Claude plugins share one set of governed capabilities.

- Make evals a first-class discipline. Design evaluation frameworks for agent and LLM behavior, including golden datasets, LLM-as-judge, human review loops, and regression suites, and run them in development and production. Use transcript analysis and eval results to find failures, guide what to fix first, and show quality improving over time.

- Lead with AI day to day. Use agents, coding assistants, and agent harnesses in your own daily work, and build the shared tooling, patterns, and harnesses that make the whole team faster.

- Stay ahead of the curve. Track new models, agent frameworks, MCP and tool ecosystems, and context engineering, and turn them into practical recommendations for Samsara's GTM use cases: what to adopt, what to test, and what to ignore. Make clear build-versus-buy calls on vendor tools, not just models.

- Drive adoption with the field. Be the go-to advocate for AI across Sales, CS, and Support. Run demos, earn credibility with reps and frontline managers, collect real feedback, and turn skeptics into power users.

- Set the strategy. Own the technical and product strategy for GTM AI, including the data foundations, instrumentation, governance, and observability these products depend on. Decide which prototypes move onto the shared platform, which merge, and which retire. Own model routing across vendors and the per-user spend controls that keep AI cost in line with value. Influence senior leaders on AI priorities, investment, and the operating model.

- Ship revenue-critical intelligence. Own the forecasting, propensity, and CRM data-quality work that sales leadership acts on, and keep it calibrated, validated, and clear about its limits. Be comfortable across data and analytics engineering, and act as a business leader when the work calls for it.

- Partner across GTM, Product, and Engineering. Work with Sales, Customer Success, Support, Enablement, Operations, Product, and Engineering leaders to find high-value opportunities, define success metrics, and turn them into durable products.

- Build for trust. Put a pragmatic responsible-AI approach in place: safety, privacy, reliability, and human-in-the-loop workflows with clear approval and escalation paths. Agents that act on CRM and customer data run with per-user, least-privilege permissions, and changes to systems of record get human approval first.

- Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

- Hire, develop and lead an inclusive, engaged, and high performing AI Engineering team

Minimum requirements for the role: 

- 10+ years across software engineering, machine learning, data science, or data platforms, including meaningful leadership experience. You still write code regularly.

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant work experience.

- Hands-on experience building and shipping LLM applications and agentic workflows to production, including tool use, retrieval, context engineering, and production reliability.

- Production full-stack and cloud engineering experience (for example Python or TypeScript, AWS, and Databricks), including owning systems that other teams depend on.

- Demonstrated experience designing and running evaluation frameworks for LLM or agent systems, and using them to drive quality decisions.

- Daily, fluent use of AI agents and coding assistants in your own work, and a point of view on how they change the way teams build.

- A track record of shipping internal or customer-facing AI/ML products with measurable business impact.

- Experience with predictive modeling, experimentation, analytics, and data engineering foundations.

- Strong product judgment and the ability to turn ambiguous business problems into simple, valuable solutions.

- Excellent communication with both executives and frontline users. You can demo to a sales floor and present to a VP on the same day.

- A people-first leadership style with a track record of hiring, developing, and keeping strong technical talent.

An ideal candidate also has: 

- Experience building AI or decisioning products for Sales, Customer Success, Support, Marketing, or other GTM functions, ideally in a fast-growing enterprise SaaS environment.

- Experience with CRM, customer data, support, and knowledge-management systems (such as Salesforce, Gong, Gainsight, Zendesk, and Databricks), and connecting agents to them (for example, through MCP servers or similar integrations).

- Experience with agent SDKs and harnesses (such as Claude Code / Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph, or similar) and LLM observability tooling, eval tooling such as Braintrust or MLflow, and model APIs from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google.

- Experience operating AI products at scale, including cost management, monitoring, and governance.

- A visible habit of learning in public, such as writing, talks, open-source work, or internal “what’s new in AI” sessions.

title: Sr. Data Engineer
description:
Headquarters: Remote

About Carrot: 

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide.

Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com .

The Opportunity 

Carrot is seeking a Sr. Data Engineer to lead the evolution, reliability, and scalability of our modern data infrastructure across analytics, reporting, and business intelligence. In this role, you will architect, build, and maintain robust, automated data pipelines, orchestrate workflows, integrate diverse data sources, and partner with stakeholders across the business to deliver secure, compliant, high-quality data solutions.

Your work will span the full data lifecycle, from architecting resilient ETL/ELT pipelines and developing real-time and batch data integrations to automating reporting, reducing technical debt, and enabling advanced analytics. Sr. Data Engineers at Carrot are operational stewards and technical mentors, driving improvements in system maturity, cost efficiency, automation, and collaborative practices.

You will join our Data Engineering team, which develops and optimizes scalable data pipelines and cloud infrastructure to enable secure, automated reporting and analytics across Carrot. The team collaborates closely with Business Intelligence, Product, Finance, Legal, and Commercial partners to deliver reliable integrations and self-serve solutions that drive business insights and operational efficiency.

What You’ll Own 

In this role, you will:

- Architect, build, test, deploy, and maintain scalable, automated ETL/ELT pipelines using Python, dbt, and orchestration tools such as Prefect and Airflow

- Administer and optimize cloud-based data warehouse and lake platforms, including Snowflake, AWS (S3, Redshift), and Google Cloud, integrating new sources and tuning for performance and cost

- Orchestrate data workflows with custom scheduling, alerting, dependency management, monitoring, and error resolution

- Design and maintain secure external data flows through SFTP, Files.com, and APIs, with a focus on reliability and compliance

- Automate manual reporting and operational tasks, building robust, reusable pipeline components that reduce operational overhead

- Partner with backend product engineers to optimize production database schemas with analytics use cases in mind

- Strengthen data quality, lineage, governance, and documentation practices across key data domains

- Mentor teammates and reinforce best practices in version control, code review, and structured workflow management

What Success Looks Like 

In your first 12–18 months, you will have:

- Taken end-to-end ownership of core pipelines and integrations, with measurable improvements in reliability, data recency, and cost efficiency

- Automated high-effort manual workflows, reducing operational risk and freeing capacity for higher-value engineering work

- Delivered secure, compliant data integrations that stakeholders across the business trust for decision-making

- Strengthened observability across the platform, including monitoring, alerting, and incident response for critical data workflows

- Established yourself as a technical mentor and a go-to partner for Business Intelligence, Product, and cross-functional teams

About You 

You likely have:

- Expert-level proficiency in Snowflake, dbt, and Python for data modeling, transformation, pipeline development, and advanced analytics

- Advanced SQL skills for complex querying, large-scale data model design, and database optimization

- Proven experience architecting, building, testing, deploying, and maintaining scalable, automated ETL/ELT pipelines using modern orchestration tools such as Prefect and Airflow

- Hands-on administration of cloud-based data warehouse and lake platforms, including Snowflake, AWS (S3, Redshift), and Google Cloud

- A strong understanding of secure external data flows through SFTP, Files.com, and APIs, with a focus on reliability and compliance

- Mastery of version control (Git, GitHub) and structured workflow management (Jira) for code review, audit trails, and operational transparency

- A demonstrated ability to automate and simplify complex manual tasks, building robust, reusable pipeline components

- Dependability, adaptability, and a collaborative approach to engineering, thriving in dynamic and ambiguous environments

Nice to Have ⭐ 

While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring:

- Hands-on experience in startup or rapid-growth environments, delivering technical solutions under shifting priorities

- A background supporting business intelligence, analytics, and data science teams through large-scale integrations and multi-tenant reporting

- Familiarity with both batch and event-driven ingestion paradigms, including near-real-time pipelines built on Snowflake, dbt, and Python

- Experience automating operational, financial, or compliance-driven workflows within cloud data environments

- Exposure to audit, privacy, and compliance frameworks such as SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, ISO, and SOX, particularly in data governance and secure access controls

- Experience in regulated industries such as healthcare, healthtech, or SaaS

Why This Role Matters 

Reliable data is the foundation of how Carrot operates, from the analytics that guide business decisions to the reporting our customers and partners depend on. The systems this role owns determine the accuracy, recency, and security of data used across the entire company.

As Carrot scales globally, the Sr. Data Engineer will make our data platform more automated, resilient, and cost-efficient, enabling teams across the business to move faster with data they trust. This work directly supports Carrot's mission of expanding access to fertility and family-building care worldwide.

Interview Process 

We believe in a thoughtful and transparent interview process designed to create alignment for both candidates and our team.

For this role, candidates can expect:

- Recruiter Screen — 30 minutes

- Hiring Manager Interview — 30–45 minutes

- Cross-Functional Panel Interviews — 45 minutes

- Executive Leadership Conversation — 30 minutes

- Hiring Manager Wrap-Up — 15 minutes

Throughout the process, we will share additional context about the team, business priorities, customer landscape, and what success looks like in this role.

Why Candidates Join Carrot 

Carrot offers the opportunity to do meaningful work in service of a deeply human mission.

Highlights include:

- A mission-driven company focused on expanding access to fertility and family-forming care globally.

- A high-growth environment where leaders are empowered to shape strategy and drive impact.

- Competitive compensation, equity, and comprehensive benefits.

- Flexible Time Off and a culture that actively encourages employees to recharge.

- Comprehensive parental leave and family-forming benefits.

- A collaborative, inclusive, and values-driven culture.

- The opportunity to work alongside passionate, thoughtful teammates committed to improving healthcare outcomes worldwide.

Compensation: 

Carrot offers a holistic Total Rewards package designed to support our employees in all aspects of their life inside and outside of work, including health and wellness benefits, retirement savings plans, short- and long-term incentives, parental leave, family-forming assistance, and a competitive compensation package. The starting base salary for this position will range from $145,000-$165,000. Actual compensation may vary from posted base salary depending on your confirmed job-related skills and experience. 

Fraud and Security Notice: Please note that all communication regarding job opportunities at Carrot will come exclusively from an @get-carrot.com email address. If you receive messages from any other domain, please disregard them and report the incident to: securityreporting@get-carrot.com 

A Note on AI 

At Carrot, we believe AI can help us work smarter, move faster, and create more meaningful experiences for our members, customers, and each other. While not every role requires deep technical AI expertise, we value people who are curious, eager to learn, and excited to thoughtfully incorporate AI into their day-to-day work.

For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement—and we'll call that out clearly in the qualifications. For everyone else, we're looking for people who embrace new ways of working, use AI responsibly to improve quality and efficiency, and continue to learn as the technology evolves.

Why Carrot? 

Carrot has received national and international recognition for its pioneering work, including Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and World Changing Ideas, Inc. Power Partners, and Modern Healthcare’s Innovators. Carrot’s global workforce has been acknowledged with several accolades, including Fortune’s Best Workplaces in Healthcare, Great Place to Work, and Age-Friendly Employer certifications. Carrot is regularly featured in media reporting on issues related to the future of work, women in leadership, and healthcare innovation, including MSNBC, The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, CNBC, National Public Radio, Harvard Business Review, and more. Learn more at carrotfertility.com.

- Strong understanding of monitoring, observability, alerting, and incident-management practices. 

- Experience with CI/CD, Git, GitHub Actions, and automation using Bash, Python, PowerShell, or similar scripting languages.

Nice to Have

- Experience with monitoring tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, or similar platforms.

- Experience with MongoDB Atlas, Ops Manager, or comparable MongoDB tooling.

Our AI Mindset

title: Senior Product Designer (m/f/d)
description:

This gives consumers better interest rates and banks a diversified form of refinancing . Our vision is to offer savings and investments without barriers and thus open up the global 160 trillion euro market.

Raisin currently employs more than 800 people from over 75 countries worldwide. Today, the platform holds over 80 billion euros in assets from more than one million investors which have accrued over 5 billion euros in returns.

Team 

The Design team at Raisin brings together product designers and brand & marketing designers; we are united by our shared belief in the power of respect, creativity, and the purpose to give people financial peace of mind. We’ve built a place where empathy and innovation thrive, where integrity and high quality standards underpin our work. We love our diversity and use the strength of our perspectives to reach our goals. 

We build with heart to create solutions that empower users, shake up industries, and leave a lasting mark, all while working to make Raisin a leader in our field.

Your Responsibilities 

Create desirable, usable digital products and features: 

- Lead design activities to launch and improve features that help customers explore and manage their portfolio or products and services offered by Raisin - and confidently move from information to action - across app, web, and email. 

- Proactively identify places where AI can simplify complex financial journeys.

- Lead rapid prototyping activities. Use generative and agentic tools to turn bold concepts into something people can try and share feedback on. 

- Co-lead - with Product Managers and Engineers - larger end-to-end design discovery and delivery.

Own design QA checks, and support implementation by contributing to-be-reviewed code (through agentic tools) for the small things that make the experience better. 

- Run feedback loops so AI-generated work meets a high ethical and quality standard.

Collaborate across functions:

- Partner with peers, engineers, and data specialists to experiment and to put in place the UX infrastructure for AI-driven features. Co-create products that are personal and highly secure.

- Tell a clear story. Explain your design intent, choices, and trade-offs to team and stakeholders. Ask for feedback, and give it clearly and openly. 

Turn technical and compliance requirements into usable experiences: 

- Translate complex backend and platform capabilities, including AI/ML models and agentic logic, into interfaces that customers and internal teams can easily use.

- Surface compliance requirements, and use them to shape experiences that are robust and friendly at the same time.

Contribute to a living design system: 

- Adopt reusable, flexible UX patterns, and add new ones when needed, so we make micro-frontends look - and feel - cohesive.

- Work closely with the team responsible for the Raisin Design System, so components and patterns stay accessible, consistent and well documented across platforms.

- Help the live design system grow: contribute spec-to-code delivery of components and scalable UX patterns when they support the features, services, and experiences you are designing.

Stay curious, and keep experimenting:

- Keep your craft fresh. Stay current on AI capabilities and on how design work changes when agents are in the loop, so Raisin’s design practice stays sharp.

Your Profile

- Experienced with prototyping using Generative and Agentic tools to accelerate concept exploration and build high-fidelity work - for both discovery and delivery.

- Mastery of execution and delivery processes, including project management and resource allocation

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. title: Applied AI Engineer, CyberSecurity, Defense
description:
About Mistral 

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

Role Summary

We are seeking an Applied AI, Forward Deployed Engineer to build customer use cases on top of the Mistral stack for our defense, government and critical-infrastructure customers. You will work with some of the most security-sensitive organizations in the world: government agencies, sovereign institutions and operators of critical infrastructure. They need AI that is powerful, controllable and deployable on their terms.

you will build some of the first AI-for-cyberdefense systems deployed in real government and defense environments, on frontier models you can influence. You will work in a tight-knit team alongside elite experts in DFIR and cyberdefense — people who are passionate about their craft — and the patterns you implement at customer sites feed directly back into Mistral's internal use cases and products. title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Evals
description:
Who We Are

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

About the team 

Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, e-commerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people.

About the role 

Evaluation is the core of everything we do. We build from the evals: we define how success will be measured before developing a capability, and use the results to guide training, model selection and deployment. We already have hundreds of evaluations spanning domain knowledge, commerce and gaming, with plans to expand their coverage, depth and scale.

This work builds on ProLLM, the public benchmarking platform we ran for real-world use cases until our coding assistant benchmarks became saturated. Since then it has been a private benchmarking platform for Prosus companies. We plan to open it again to publish our commerce benchmarks, covering both agentic and decision-making tasks.

We’re looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to own the development of these evaluations and the platform that runs them. The work involves defining meaningful tasks, curating evaluation data, implementing reliable scoring, investigating model behaviour and making results useful for research and product decisions.

In our flat team of around 30 engineers, you’ll work directly with applied scientists, training engineers and domain experts. You’ll help teams contribute evaluations and build the infrastructure and automation needed to run them throughout model development.

In the first three months, we expect you to take technical ownership of part of the evaluation platform, deliver a set of new or improved evaluations with curated data and calibrated difficulty, and work with scientists to use them in a training or release decision.

What the role involves 

- Design evaluations with scientists and domain experts, translating intended capabilities into representative tasks, datasets and success criteria. Cover current applications and capabilities we want future models to acquire.

- Curate evaluation data and calibrate task difficulty, so that evaluations are neither saturated nor out of reach and still separate models of different quality. Work with domain experts on sourcing, annotation and review, within data provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy requirements.

- Own the development and operation of the evaluation platform across training checkpoints, deployed models and external baselines. Support distributed execution, reproducible configurations, trace inspection and comparison of results, while managing runtime and cost.

- Develop programmatic checks, outcome-based scoring and LLM-based graders. Calibrate automated judgments against expert reviews, investigate disagreements and test whether graders reward superficial answers or reject valid solutions.

- Analyse model outputs and agent trajectories, including tool calls, environment state and task outcomes. Distinguish model failures from problems in the evaluation, quantify uncertainty and explain what changed between versions.

- Maintain versioned tasks, datasets, graders and environments, with protected held-out tests and contamination checks. Expand coverage as models improve, retaining useful regression tests and adding harder tasks where existing tests no longer distinguish performance.

- Prepare commerce benchmarks for public release on ProLLM, including public mirror sets and evaluation code, where the data can be shared.

- Integrate evaluations into training and release workflows, with dashboards and regression checks that support concrete decisions. Work with portfolio teams to establish whether offline improvements correspond to better outcomes in online experiments.

- Build tools and agents that help generate candidate tasks, run evaluations and investigate failures, validating their outputs before adoption. Review contributions and mentor engineers so teams can extend the suite consistently.

Minimum qualifications 

- At least five years of ML or software engineering experience, including substantial hands-on work building and evaluating ML systems.

- Experience owning evaluation frameworks, benchmarks or model-quality systems that informed training or deployment decisions.

- Strong Python and experience with PyTorch, Transformers or comparable ML libraries, alongside reliable production software development.

- Practical knowledge of experimental design and statistics, including sampling, uncertainty, repeated trials and comparisons across model versions.

- Experience running inference or evaluation workloads at scale and debugging failures across models, data, scoring code and infrastructure.

- Clear communication and the ability to turn ambiguous results into defensible recommendations.

Preferred qualifications 

- Experience with language-model training or post-training.

- Experience with agent or gaming environments.

- Experience with human evaluation, LLM-as-judge calibration, recommendation metrics or online experimentation.

- Contributions to evaluation frameworks, public benchmarks or research.

What we offer 

- Ownership of the evaluation platform and the evaluations that guide LCM’s research, training and deployment.

- Access to proprietary domain data, GPU infrastructure and external models for comparison.

- Direct collaboration with researchers, engineers and portfolio teams, with scope to publish methods and benchmarks, including through ProLLM, where the work can be shared.

- Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems.

- Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants.

- A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role.

- Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro.

If you want to build the evaluations that shape what a foundation model learns, we’d like to hear from you. Please include examples of evaluations or platforms you have built, how you established that their results were reliable, and the decisions those results informed.

Why Prosus? 

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.

Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing.

Our Diversity & Inclusion Commitment 

We respect the dignity and human rights of individuals and communities wherever we operate in the world. Building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome and can thrive is critical for us. We provide access to education, which helps everyone understand the important role they play and the positive impact they can have.
