title: AI Platform Engineer
description:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We are hiring a AI Platform Engineer to build the execution layer for Supabase's internal AI systems.

Supabase is building an AI-native internal operating system: a common way of working across the company where AI carries a meaningful share of the operational load rather than sitting alongside it as an assistant. We are standing up a new central team to build those systems, enable the teams, and embed AI operations throughout the organization. You are the engineer on that team.

The execution layer is yours. You will build the platform that actually runs agents: an event-triggered queue, a headless model-agnostic runtime, durable state so work survives a restart, a human review gate, atomic rollback, and full logging of every prompt, tool call and decision so any run can be reconstructed. You will build the evaluation layer that makes any of it trustworthy, because an agent that cannot be measured cannot be trusted with anything beyond reading. And you will build the agents themselves, across everything from executive reporting down to a layer of agents that watch the platform and improve it.

This is a governance-heavy environment by design, and that is the interesting part of the problem. Agents are risk-tiered from read-only internal data through to external-facing output, with review depth, evaluation requirements and human approval scaling by tier. Some capabilities are permanently off limits: an agent may read and report, it may carry a human-authored update into a system of record once a human consents, and it may initiate contact within a strict budget, but it may never autonomously write a commitment (an owner, a due date, a status) into a shared work system. Your job is to make that structurally impossible rather than merely forbidden.

You will be the only engineer on this platform. You will close open architecture decisions yourself, own the infrastructure end to end, and instrument the system so it reports its own return.

What You'll Be Responsible For

In this role, you'll:

- 
Ship the agent platform to production. An event-triggered queue, a headless model-agnostic runtime (choosing the runtime is an open decision you will close), durable state that survives a failed run, a human review gate, atomic rollback, and complete run logging in the warehouse.

- 
Own the evaluation layer, and switch on the gate that depends on it. Golden suites with behavioral assertions rather than intuition, judge criteria with a written rubric, safety cases that must pass on every run, and a CI gate that blocks a regression from merging. This is the precondition for every agent that does anything beyond read internal data.

- 
Build and register the agent portfolio. Reporting, drafting, linting, triage and question-answering agents across the executive, team-lead and individual-contributor layers, plus a meta layer that observes the platform and improves it.

- 
Enforce governance in code. Risk tiers the pipeline actually enforces, least-privilege credentials per agent, tool-permission gates, a decision audit log, and autonomy classes where the dangerous class has no code path rather than a warning label. Nothing runs without a registered owner, tier, tool grant and human gate.

- 
Design how the system contacts people. A hard interruption budget per person, message bundling instead of a stream of pings, and a structure that gives something useful before it asks for anything. Adoption depends on this more than on any other single design choice.

- 
Own the platform tooling. The compiler and validator, inventory integrity, and the paths that distribute context and capabilities into the repositories and chat surfaces where work happens.

- 
Compute the operating measures from production data. A pipeline from raw system activity through to a computed maturity grade per team, defensible enough that a team can dispute the result and be answered with the query rather than an opinion.

- 
Instrument the platform's own return. A ledger that logs the work each agent absorbs and computes the monthly figure, so the value of the system is a measurement rather than a claim.

How You'll Think

Recursive Thinking

You build the generator, not the artifact. When you need thirty agents, you do not write thirty agents; you build the inventory, the compiler and the distribution path that makes the thirty-first cost an afternoon, then a meta layer whose job is to watch the platform, find its drift and file the fix.

The evaluation layer is the same move applied to trust. You are not checking whether one agent is correct today. You are building the machine that decides whether every future agent is allowed to ship, which means the suite has to be right in a way the agent does not, and the thing that grades has to be graded too.

Inversion Thinking

You start from the failure and work backward to the design. The rule is that an agent may never autonomously write a commitment into a shared work system. The weak implementation is an instruction in a prompt. The strong one is that the credential in the agent's tool grant physically cannot set an owner, a due date or a status, so no amount of clever input, prompt injection or model error produces the forbidden write. You reach for the second one first.

Same for evaluation. Before writing a suite you enumerate how the agent can be wrong: an update that invents progress that did not happen, one that quotes a private channel into a public digest, one that is accurate and reads as an accusation, one that credits the wrong person. Then the suite is that list, each case caught before the agent ships rather than after it embarrasses someone.

AI-Native Execution

You use agentic tools on real work, in files and repositories, with the same rigor you apply to anything else you ship. You have a setup of your own and can describe it mechanically: what triggers it, what it is allowed to touch, where the human approves, what it logs, and how you found out the one time it went wrong.

That experience is this job, generalized. You are building for async engineers across 40+ countries who will judge the platform by whether it saves them an hour or costs them one, so you are your own first user and your own harshest reviewer.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

Must Have

- 
Have shipped production LLM agent systems that other people depended on. Not demos, not internal showcases. Systems with operational history, real users and at least one incident you can talk through. Prompt engineering on its own does not clear this bar.

- 
Design evaluations, not spot checks. You build golden sets, write behavioral assertions, define judge rubrics, set pass thresholds and gate CI on the result. You can explain why "we reviewed a bunch of outputs and they looked good" is not evaluation.

- 
Have done deep API work against the systems work actually lives in , and have authored MCP servers. You know the specific failure modes of those APIs, not just that they exist.

- 
Own infrastructure end to end in Python on GCP, with a cloud warehouse and infrastructure as code. You provision, deploy, monitor and roll back your own systems, and you close architecture decisions rather than routing them onward.

- 
Have taste about how software contacts humans. You treat every notification as spending a limited amount of trust.

Strong Signal

- 
Public work in this space. An open-source agent framework, an MCP server, an evaluation harness, or writing on agent reliability that other practitioners cite.

- 
LLM observability and cost instrumentation. Tracing agent runs, attributing spend per run, and building the queries that turn raw logs into a report someone acts on.

- 
You have built an internal platform that non-engineers adopted voluntarily , and can describe what you changed after watching them use it.

What Success Looks Like

- 
The platform is boring. Agents run on a schedule and on events, state survives restarts, failed runs roll back cleanly, and every run can be reconstructed from its log.

- 
Nothing ships unevaluated. Every registered agent has a real suite with safety cases, the gate blocks regressions, and when someone challenges an output the answer is a test case rather than an argument.

- 
The dangerous action is impossible, not discouraged. An audit of any agent's credentials shows it cannot perform the writes it is not allowed to perform, and the audit log makes every consequential decision traceable.

- 
Teams pull the platform instead of being pushed. Agents get adopted because the reports are useful and the contact is rare and well-timed, and each team ends up with at least one workflow that runs automatically.

- 
The platform reports its own value. The work absorbed is measured and published, so the case for expanding it is made with data rather than enthusiasm.

What We Offer 

- 
Fully Remote 

We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

- 
ESOP 

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

- 
Tech Allowance 

Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

- 
Health Benefits 

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

- 
Annual Off-Sites 

Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

- 
Flexible Work 

We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

- 
Professional Development 

Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team 

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

- 
~400 team members

- 
60+ countries

- 
20+ languages spoken

- 
Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

- 
540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. 

An overview of this role 

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer (Python) in GitLab's Agent Foundations stage, you'll go beyond using AI tools. You'll help build the foundations for GitLab's agentic AI experiences: the platform that lets AI agents work across the whole software delivery lifecycle, not just write code. That covers the reusable building blocks agents and flows are made from as well as our core harness, Duo Developer.

Most of your work will be backend engineering in Python, using libraries such as LangGraph to build secure, reliable and scalable features in our AI Gateway. You'll also work across the stack where needed. You'll work closely with engineers across the stage and other AI Engineering teams. This is a high-visibility area where GitLab's core platform meets its AI strategy.

What you'll do 

- Develop, ship and maintain features for the Duo Agent Platform in the Duo Workflow Service, the AI Gateway and, where needed, the GitLab monolith. Keep them secure, well-tested and performant.

- Build and improve agentic flows and their reusable parts with LangChain and LangGraph, including the Flow Registry.

- Work with Product Management, UX, frontend, backend and AI specialists to refine requirements and ship improvements in small iterations.

- Design, implement and review APIs (including GraphQL and REST) and the backend logic behind them, with reliable, scalable and clear contracts for clients such as the GitLab monolith, IDE extensions and Duo CLI.

- Improve and extend automated testing (pytest and other frameworks), including evaluations of agent and flow behavior, to strengthen quality and give developers faster feedback.

- Share standards, patterns and learnings with other engineers to raise the bar for responsible AI integration and evidence-driven engineering.

- Join Tier 2 on-call rotations to troubleshoot production issues, contribute to root cause analysis, and improve observability and resiliency.

- Keep an eye on the competitive landscape to help keep GitLab's agent platform best-in-class as more work becomes agentic.

What you'll bring 

- Experience building and maintaining production Python backend applications, including APIs, asynchronous or background processing, and data models.

- Experience with LLM application frameworks such as LangGraph, or designing and shipping AI-powered backend features or harnesses.

- Skill in designing or extending APIs (REST, GraphQL or gRPC) with attention to scalability, maintainability and backward compatibility.

The Agent Foundations stage builds the foundations for GitLab's agentic AI experiences. Between them, they own the GitLab Duo Developer foundational flow and the Flow Registry; the AI Catalog, including custom agents, custom flows and external agent integrations; and agent execution, agent tools and agent observability.

Our engineers work async-first across EMEA, AMER, and India timezones. We work with teams across AI engineering and the rest of GitLab so the Duo Agent Platform can power many of GitLab's AI features.

title: Software Engineer, Research Platform
description:
Software Engineer, Research Platform

About Us

Basecamp Research is building frontier AI for therapeutic design. We believe the future of medicine lies in reprogramming the body to repair itself, and we design the models and the medicines to teach it how.

Our EDEN models are trained on BaseData and our Trillion Gene Atlas (TGA), the world's largest proprietary genomic dataset, with over 10B genes collected through partnerships in more than 30 countries across all seven continents. This gives our AI models access to genetic diversity that doesn't exist in public databases, and enables EDEN to design cell and gene therapies, enzymes, and peptides directly from information about a disease. Our pipeline of EDEN-designed therapeutics, beginning with in vivo cell therapy, is advancing towards clinical development.

In September 2026 we closed an oversubscribed $140M Series C led by S32, with participation from NVIDIA, Anthropic's Anthology Fund, Catalio, European Tech Collective, Firebrand River Capital, King Philanthropies, NATO Innovation Fund, NVentures (NVIDIA's venture arm), Redalpine, Rockefeller Foundation, Singular, Sovereign AI and True Ventures. We have offices and labs in London and Boston, we partner with biopharma companies and academic institutions worldwide, and our work has been recognised by Fast Company's Top 10 Most Innovative Companies in Biotech, the FT-backed Sifted AI100 list of Europe's leading AI startups as well as Barclays Eagle Labs Ones to watch, AI100.

At Basecamp Research, we pride ourselves on being a lean collaborative and global team with extremely specialist and unique skills. Our biologists, engineers, ML scientists and field explorers are united by a sense of adventure and the belief that AI, biology and data, will result in new medicines for patients who have few options today.

The Role

We're seeking an exceptional Software Engineer, Research Platform to join our team in London, embedded in our AI, genomics and computational biology teams. Your goal is to accelerate their research by bringing production-grade engineering to the systems they depend on.

This is an embedded role. You'll sit with the scientists, understand what they are trying to find out, and build the systems that get them there faster: making research code reliable, reproducible and fast; designing data pipelines and workflows that run at the scale of BaseData and the Trillion Gene Atlas; and building the tools and infrastructure that let a small research team run far more experiments. You'll move between genomics, computational biology and ML work as the research requires, and own what you build end to end.

The engineering problems are substantial: petascale biological data, workflows that span cloud and HPC, and research that is often limited by how quickly an idea can be turned into a result.

You'll report to the Head of Platform as part of our engineering team, which spans London and Boston, and work day to day within the AI research, genomics and computational biology teams in London.

About you

- A very strong engineering background: complex production systems you have designed, built and owned. Expert in Python; strong habits around testing, code review and CI/CD.

- You take responsibility for the outcome. If that means learning something new or working outside your usual area, you do it.

- A solid understanding of data pipelines, workflow orchestration, distributed execution and scalable compute (Kubernetes, HPC, containers).

- You can take a researcher's code, understand the question behind it, and make it robust without losing what made it useful.

- A real interest in biology, ideally with experience of genomic, protein or sequencing data. You will learn the science well enough to understand the research, not just its code.

- Collaborative and low ego. We care about drive, and in a small team everyone depends on what you build.

Nice to have

- Research or applied experience in computational biology, bioinformatics or genomics.

- Experience with bioinformatics tooling and sequencing data at scale.

- Familiarity with Dagster or similar orchestration, Kubernetes, cloud and HPC compute.

- Experience building tools, MCP servers or workflows that AI agents and researchers use to run computational experiments.

What we offer in return

Impactful Mission: This is a rare chance to do work that genuinely matters. You'll join a talented, fast-moving team, access unique biological datasets at scale, and see your contributions shape real breakthroughs in AI and curative therapeutics.

Collaborative Culture: You'll be surrounded by world-class engineers, scientists, and researchers who care deeply about their work and about each other. With offices in London and Boston, we've built a flexible, cross-functional environment where personal development and real ownership aren't just talking points.

High Growth: We truly believe in investing in our top talent, we make coaching available to team members during steep growth journeys and we have twice yearly promotion opportunities. People who are really successful here own it and go directly to solve problems at pace and we ensure reward increases with impact.

Comprehensive Benefits: We've built a benefits package people value. That means competitive salary, equity, and private healthcare with no medical history exclusions so strong that most employees' family members opt into our plan over their own. We also offer Carrot Fertility with IVF stipend, salary sacrifice pension, bike to work scheme, life insurance, and more.

Do you want to join our team as our new Software Engineer, Research Platform? Then we'd love to hear from you.

We are committed to equal opportunity employment regardless of ethnic or national origin, race, religion, sex, age, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, gender identity or any other basis. If you have a disability or additional need that needs accommodating do let us know.

title: Engineering Lead, Clinical Operations
description:
At Clover, the Business Enablement team leads our technological advancement while ensuring robust security and compliance. We deliver user-friendly corporate applications, manage complex data ecosystems, and provide efficient tech solutions across the organization. Our goal is simple: we make it easy for the business to do what’s right for Clover.

We’re hiring a Engineering Lead to build the systems that help our clinical teams deliver services in the field and in members’ homes. You will own technical direction and delivery for scheduling, dispatch, field and mobile workflows, and the software that connects equipment and home technology to the operation.

A likely first assignment is an “Air Traffic Control” system for field operations. A supervisor needs to understand what is happening and act when the plan breaks: a flat tire, a delayed visit, a missing piece of equipment, or a member whose availability changes. You will work with the people doing the job to decide what they need to see, what the system can help resolve, and when a human should intervene.

This is a hands-on role that spans product and engineering. You will understand the business problem, shape the solution, build useful increments, and see whether they work. You may start without direct reports and can expect to coach and eventually manage one or two engineers. You should enjoy building personally and helping others become more capable.

We value a tinkering instinct: try the unfamiliar tool, inspect the data, trace the failure, put a small improvement in front of a user, and learn from what happens. Hardware or connected-device experience can be a strong signal of that mindset, but it is not required. The central work is building dependable software for an operation that changes throughout the day.

As an Engineering Lead, Clinical Operations, you will: 

- Work directly with supervisors, clinical field staff, and operations leaders to understand schedules, travel, capacity, handoffs, and the exceptions that disrupt a day’s work.

- Build field visibility and intervention tools that give supervisors useful context, distinguish current facts from missing information, and help them respond to changing conditions.

- Develop scheduling and dispatch capabilities that match people and visits to practical constraints, with clear ways for operating staff to review and adjust the plan.

- Build and debug APIs, mobile workflows, integrations, and data flows supporting field teams, connected equipment, and home technology.

- Prototype quickly and ship focused increments. Make deliberate choices about what to build, integrate, or buy, and avoid committing to a large system before the operation has tested the approach.

- Use AI actively for development, investigation, prototypes, analysis, and useful workflow capabilities. Check the behavior and make failures understandable and recoverable.

- Coach engineers and take on a small number of direct reports as the team develops. Maintain clear ownership, sound engineering practices, and credible delivery commitments.

- Partner with Product, Special Project Leads, IT, Counterpart, and the Engagement lead at the interfaces their work shares with field operations.

Success in this role looks like: 

- First 90 days: You understand how the field operation works, have shipped an improvement used by supervisors or field staff, and can show what it changed. You have a focused technical plan grounded in real constraints and exceptions.

- First six months: Several useful increments are in place. Supervisors can understand and respond to disruptions more effectively, scheduling and field workflows are improving, and technical ownership is clear.

You should get in touch if: 

- You are a strong production software engineer who has owned meaningful work end-to-end and still builds regularly.

- You can move across backend services, APIs, data flows, user interfaces, and operational workflows to solve a real problem.

- You have strong product instincts, learn unfamiliar domains directly, and enjoy working with the people using what you build.

- You have an iterative, curious approach to technology. You can describe an unfamiliar system you explored, a practical prototype you tried, or a failure you traced across boundaries.

- You use AI in your own engineering work and have practical experience building or integrating AI-backed capabilities, with clear verification and evaluation.

- You can coach engineers and are interested in responsibility for a small team as it develops. Formal management experience can help, but a strong record of Engineering Leadership and coaching also matters.

Benefits Overview : 

- Financial Well-Being : Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.

- Physical Well-Being : We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.

- Mental Well-Being : We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, monthly company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous flexible time-off policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location. 

- Professional Development : Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Additional Perks: 

- Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offering discounted equity opportunities

- Reimbursement for office setup expenses

- Monthly cell phone & internet stipend

- Remote-first culture, enabling collaboration with global teams

- Paid parental leave for all new parents

- And much more!

About Clover: We are reinventing health insurance by combining the power of data with human empathy to keep our members healthier. We believe the healthcare system is broken, so we've created custom software and analytics to empower our clinical staff to intervene and provide personalized care to the people who need it most.

We always put our members first, and our success as a team is measured by the quality of life of the people we serve. Those who work at Clover are passionate and mission-driven individuals with diverse areas of expertise, working together to solve the most complicated problem in the world: healthcare.

From Clover’s inception, Diversity & Inclusion have always been key to our success. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, perspectives, opinions, and backgrounds, who share a passion for improving people's lives. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employee’s points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

title: Growth Associate
description:
As Sales Development Representative, you sit at the front of how Electric Twin grows. You decide which accounts deserve our attention, get us into rooms with the people who run insights, brand and strategy at large organisations, and hand the sales team conversations worth having.

You'll report into Sales with a dotted line into Marketing. Lead generation comes from Marketing, so there is a steady flow of inbound interest, event contacts and campaign responses to work. Your job is to turn that flow, plus your own account research and outbound, into qualified meetings that convert.

This is a broad remit for an Growth Associate. You won't just be working a queue. You'll own the territory map, decide where the effort goes, and build the outbound systems that make the next quarter easier than the last.

It suits someone early in a sales career who is genuinely curious about how large organisations make decisions, comfortable writing to senior people, and organised enough to run a patch rather than react to whatever lands in the inbox.

What You'll Do 

- Own the TAM map. Build and maintain our view of the total addressable market: who fits the ICP, how many of them there are, and where the concentration sits by sector, geography and company size. Keep it current as the product and the category move. This is the document the rest of GTM plans against.

Identify and work focus accounts for ABM. Choose the named accounts worth a coordinated push. Research the buying group inside each one: who owns insights, who owns the budget, who feels the pain. Work with Marketing to sequence air cover and outbound so an account hears from us in a joined-up way. You will also own the ABM motion, ensuring the demand we drive on top of the funnel by sector is harnessed downstream and turned into leads. 

Map signals to the funnel. Define the signals that tell us an account is in motion: leadership changes in insights or brand, hiring patterns, funding, agency reviews, content engagement, event attendance, competitor mentions. Then map those signals onto the funnel so we know where our ABM accounts sit and how they move through the funnel. You will co-ordinate with our growth lead to execute focused ABM campaigns for those insights. An account that has read one blog post needs something different from one whose Head of Insights has just downloaded the accuracy whitepaper. Getting that routing right is what ensures we deliver relevance at scale.

Run outbound that sounds like a person. Build and run multichannel sequences across email, Lemlist, LinkedIn and phone. Write plainly, in first person, with a real reason for the message and a low-stakes ask. Test angles, track what earns replies, and retire what doesn't.

Turn events into pipeline. Work with Marketing on the conferences, roundtables and industry events we attend. Build the target invite list, run pre-event outreach to book meetings into the diary, work the room on the day, and drive the follow-up afterwards so every conversation is logged and progressed. Events only pay back if someone owns the week after them.

Set up and qualify meetings. Run first conversations that establish whether there is a real problem, a budget, a timeline and a route to a decision. Qualify honestly, including out. A well-reasoned disqualification is worth more to the team than a meeting that wastes an AE's afternoon.

Hand over properly. Brief the AE before every meeting: what the account does, what triggered the conversation, who is in the room, what they said, and what good looks like from here. Stay close after handover so nothing stalls in the gap.

Keep HubSpot clean. Log activity, maintain accurate contact and account records, and keep pipeline stages honest. Our forecasting, our signal routing and our marketing attribution all rest on what you enter.

Close the loop with Marketing. You'll hear objections, language and competitor mentions before anyone else. Feed that back so campaigns, content and messaging reflect what the market is actually saying. Flag which sources produce meetings that convert and which produce noise.

Tools you'll use 

- We run a full AI stack and we expect whoever takes this role to get properly fluent in it, then push it further than we have.

HubSpot for CRM, pipeline and reporting. Clay for enrichment, list building and capturing the signals that drive account routing. lemlist and Instantly for outbound sequencing and deliverability. n8n and similar workflow automation for joining the stack together so data moves without anyone copying it by hand. Claude Code for building your own tooling: research agents, enrichment scripts, briefing generators, whatever removes the repetitive part of the job.

We'd rather hire someone who reads the docs and builds the automation than someone who arrives already knowing every logo on that list.

title: Data Engineer
description:
Data Engineer 

London (Waterloo) · Full-time · Hybrid, three days per week in the office

Who we are 

At GetGround, our mission is to make property investment safer, faster and more accessible for everyone.

We’ve built an all-in-one property investment platform that supports investors from opportunity analysis and company formation through to financing, accounting and portfolio management. By bringing software, data and specialist services into one experience, we make property investing simpler, clearer and more cost-effective.

We’re now building the intelligence layer that will help investors understand opportunities, make better decisions and manage their portfolios. We bring together detailed knowledge of our customers’ investments, services such as mortgages, lettings and insurance, and a team that lives and breathes property.

We’re turning our property expertise into an intelligence layer that can scale. That starts with a data platform: selecting trusted sources, keeping information current and making it useful to our products and AI agents.

We’re looking for someone to own that foundation.

The opportunity 

You’ll define and build the data platform that powers GetGround’s intelligence layer. This is a hands-on role with substantial architectural ownership: choosing how we ingest, structure, curate and serve data, while improving the foundations we already have.

The scope goes beyond integrating with APIs. You’ll build ways to ingest unstructured policy updates, regulatory guidance and published documents, turning them into reliable data our intelligence layer can use.

You’ll work closely with engineering, product and our property experts to turn domain knowledge into useful data. You’ll also design for international expansion, so entering each new market builds on a shared platform.

There’s an opportunity to influence how we build our data organisation over time, including the capabilities, standards and future hires we need.

What you’ll do 

- Own data as a product. Start with the decisions our customers and AI agents need to make, then work backwards to the data required. Judge success by the usefulness and reliability of what you enable.

- Be opinionated about sources and quality. Work with our property experts to identify the most valuable datasets and assess their authority, coverage, freshness and limitations. Establish clear standards for what enters the platform and how conflicting information is handled.

- Build ingestion beyond APIs. Develop reliable pipelines for structured datasets, external APIs, documents and published guidance. Ingest updates from sources such as HMRC and other relevant authorities, detecting changes promptly and turning them into usable, traceable data.

- Make data usable by our intelligence layer. Structure and serve information so our products and AI agents can retrieve the right facts in context. Preserve source provenance, geographic scope and effective dates so consumers can distinguish current information from historical or superseded guidance.

- Design for international expansion. Build shared models and ingestion patterns that accommodate differences in property markets, tax systems and regulation. When we expand geographies, we want to go at speed, without rebuilding the platform.

- Own reliability throughout the lifecycle. Build monitoring, validation and recovery into ingestion, transformation, storage and serving. Know what is stale, missing or incorrect, understand the customer impact and address the root cause.

- Set the technical direction and deliver it. Make clear trade-offs between immediate product needs and long-term architecture. Ship useful improvements early, document decisions and help shape the standards and future team needed to support the platform.

What you bring 

- Experience owning substantial data systems. You’ve designed, built and operated production data platforms or major parts of them, and can explain the architectural decisions you made and their consequences.

- Strong engineering fundamentals . You bring strong SQL, data modelling and production programming skills, with practical experience in orchestration, testing, deployment and operating reliable pipelines.

- Judgment about the data itself. You can evaluate whether a source is fit for a particular use, reconcile inconsistent information and make uncertainty or gaps visible to downstream consumers.

- Experience with messy external sources. You’ve handled inconsistent formats, changing schemas, incomplete records, rate limits and integration failures. You’re comfortable working beyond clean, well-documented APIs.

- A product mindset. You care about the decisions your data supports. You can work with domain experts and product engineers to translate an ambiguous need into a useful data product.

- Architectural ownership. You can review an existing system, establish a direction and deliver improvements incrementally. You understand access controls, privacy and the responsibilities that come with combining customer and external data.

- Clear communication and initiative . You surface problems early, write down decisions and challenge assumptions constructively. You’re comfortable making progress without a fully specified ticket.

Bonus 

- Experience building data foundations for AI products, including retrieval, document processing or evaluating the quality of information supplied to agents.

- Experience modelling policy or regulatory information, including versioning and effective dates.

- Experience with property, financial services, geospatial data or international datasets.

- Familiarity with GCP, where we run our infrastructure, and experience working alongside backend engineering teams.

- Experience establishing data standards or helping build a data team.

This role isn’t for you if 

- You just want to keep the pipelines running. You’ll need to care about which data we use, whether it can be trusted and how it improves the decisions our products support.

- You want a fully specified architecture to implement. We need someone who can assess what exists, challenge assumptions and take ownership of the technical direction.

- You only want to work with clean, structured data . Important information arrives through documents, policy announcements and inconsistent external sources. Making it usable is part of the job.

- You want to stay removed from the product or domain. You’ll work closely with product engineers and property experts. Understanding what the data means and how it is used is essential.

- You don’t connect with how we work. Our values—No BS, pursuit of excellence, feedback obsessed and healthy ego—mean communicating directly, holding a high bar, seeking feedback and being willing to change your mind.

Why join 

- Own a data platform central to GetGround’s next phase of product development.

- Turn deep property expertise into intelligence that helps real investors.

- Work on challenging problems across customer data, property information, AI and regulated services.

- Shape the architecture for international expansion and help build our future data organisation.

- Competitive salary and meaningful equity.

- Hybrid London working, with three days per week in Waterloo.

- Benefits include private health and dental cover, a learning budget, a home-office setup budget and 12 mental health days per year.

What we are building: The first end-to-end real estate investment offering - making the dream of owning real estate more accessible to everyone globally.

title: Principal Applied AI Scientist, Commerce Foundation Models
description:
Who We Are 

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

About the team

Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, ecommerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people.

About the role

We’re looking for an experienced applied scientist to help set LCM’s research direction and work directly on its most demanding scientific problems. This is a hands-on individual contributor role in a flat team of around 30 engineers, with no direct reports. You will mentor colleagues and contribute to hiring, but you will not manage people.

We define how a capability will be evaluated before developing it, and use that evidence to guide training and deployment decisions. You will help decide which research questions deserve investment, design and run experiments, and develop training methods that can be used across applications.

The role requires deep expertise in a core area of model training and the judgment to connect that work with decisions about data, evaluation and deployment. Scientists and engineers work together from the first experiment through to production evaluation, and you will take scientific responsibility for agreed research projects.

A central research goal is to learn from a continuous stream of billions of user sessions across the portfolio and turn useful signals into regular updates to model weights.

What the role involves

- Develop the research agenda with the team, identifying questions that affect model quality, training efficiency or downstream results. Use experiments to decide which approaches warrant larger training runs and which should be revised or stopped.

- Lead selected research projects through implementation, training and evaluation, staying directly involved in writing code, inspecting data, debugging runs and analysing failures.

- Establish evaluation methods that separate real improvements from leakage, noise and benchmark overfitting, and work with portfolio teams to test whether offline gains hold in controlled online experiments.

- Mentor scientists and engineers through joint research, experiment reviews and technical discussion, and advise on work that crosses project boundaries.

- Contribute to hiring, publish research and support the release of models, benchmarks and training methods where the work and data can be shared.

Research areas

The initial focus will depend on your expertise and the team’s priorities. We expect substantial depth in one of the two areas below, with the ability to contribute to decisions across the other.

Pre-training and representations 

We continue pre-training open-weight models on commerce data. Research questions include how to represent users and catalogues, how to combine data from different businesses, and how to allocate compute effectively. Work may include:

- Studying data mixtures, scaling behaviour and training schedules to guide the next run.

- Designing sequences from user histories, merchant catalogues and market data, including alignment between text and semantic IDs for users, items and merchants.

- Developing mid-training methods for capability acquisition, context extension and retention of general capabilities.

- Evaluating synthetic data and distillation methods through controlled experiments, including the trade-offs between quality, inference cost and latency.

- Studying transfer across languages, markets and commerce categories, with evaluations for new users and items and for performance on future data.

- Tabular foundation models are a possible specialisation, including pre-training and in-context learning on structured commerce data.

Post-training and continual learning 

We train LCM for commerce tasks and a range of agent applications, including customer-facing assistants and agents that carry out business operations. We also develop continual learning methods that turn new interactions into regular updates to model weights. Work may include:

- Developing supervised fine-tuning, preference optimisation and reinforcement learning methods, using verifiable outcomes or learned reward models.

- Turning session histories, searches, clicks, purchases, repeat orders and operator feedback into training examples and rewards, accounting for exposure bias, delayed feedback and the difference between observed engagement and incremental business value.

- Studying data selection, replay and update frequency so models learn from new interactions without losing established capabilities.

- Training and evaluating decision models that choose rankings, offers and promotions, using offline learning and off-policy evaluation to estimate policy value and uncertainty and inform controlled online experiments.

- Training models for multi-turn conversations and multi-step agent workflows, including understanding user intent, planning, tool use, maintaining context, recovering from errors and verifying outcomes. This includes building RL environments with simulated users and catalogues, and testing whether gains transfer to real interactions within defined permissions and business rules.

- Calibrating reward models and LLM-based graders against expert judgments and observed outcomes, and investigating reward hacking and other unintended effects.

- Developing automated experimentation methods that propose and test changes to training recipes, prompts, tools or agent control flow, with held-out evaluations and regression checks.

How we evaluate the work

Research should produce evidence that supports a training or deployment decision. We use strong baselines, including existing production systems, and weigh model quality against compute requirements, inference cost and latency.

Experiments should be reproducible, with ablations, uncertainty estimates and failure analysis. They must account for temporal leakage, changes in the data distribution and differences between companies and markets. Negative results are valuable when they explain a limitation or stop further investment in an approach that does not work.

The work also involves data provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy-aware handling of customer histories, together with our data and engineering teams.

In the first three months, we expect you to establish a focused research programme, resolve an important training or evaluation question, and work with the relevant teams to test the resulting method in a downstream application.

Minimum qualifications

- A PhD or equivalent industry research experience in machine learning, computer science, statistics or a related field.

- At least eight years of research or applied science experience in machine learning, including doctoral research, with at least four years leading research directions that were published or reached production.

- Substantial experience developing and training models, with deep expertise in pre-training, post-training or reinforcement learning relevant to the areas above.

- A record of original contributions, shown through research papers, released models, benchmarks, open-source projects or significant advances in deployed systems.

- Scientific leadership: choosing research directions, resolving difficult technical questions and helping experienced colleagues make better decisions.

- Sound experimental and statistical judgment, including examples where the evidence changed your approach and the ability to recognise when the evidence does not support a conclusion.

- Strong Python and PyTorch skills and the ability to work independently in a shared research codebase. Research on large language models requires hands-on experience with distributed training.

- Clear communication and a collaborative approach to disagreement, review and mentoring.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with recommender systems, generative retrieval, semantic IDs, continual learning, synthetic data, distillation or tabular foundation models.

- Familiarity with commerce data and online experimentation.

- We do not expect expertise in every area.

What we offer

- Influence over LCM’s research agenda and which questions the team invests in.

- Proprietary commerce data, B300 and H200 GPUs for large-scale training, and external models for evaluation and benchmarking.

- The opportunity to take research from early experiments through publication and deployment, working directly with portfolio teams on products used by millions of people.

- Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems.

- An uncapped budget to recruit and mentor research interns for your projects, with access to candidates through our connections with leading universities.

- Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants.

- A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role.

- Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro.

How to apply

Please include examples of research or deployed work that show your contribution, the decisions involved and the evidence used to evaluate the results, and indicate which research area best matches your depth.

Why Prosus? 

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.

Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing.

Our Diversity & Inclusion Commitment 

We respect the dignity and human rights of individuals and communities wherever we operate in the world. Building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome and can thrive is critical for us. We provide access to education, which helps everyone understand the important role they play and the positive impact they can have.

title: Senior Applied AI Engineer, Document Intelligence

About the role

For 40 years Vertican has buildt software that runs law firms. One year ago we created a new modern AI platform for document automation (processing/extraction/redacting) which our customers have been adopting faster than any product we've ever had. Our suite of AI-enabled products save customers thousands of hours each week by processing high volumes of documents with precision and speed.The AI team is growing and we'd like you to join.

We are hiring an engineer to own the document processing pipelines end to end: design, benchmarking, experimenting with new architectures and tools, threshold required for deploying a new pipeline, etc.

We believe it's important to build our own tooling to help us run, improve, and measure our applications. Therefore, the ideal candidate thinks outside the box on how to not just build the product/pipeline, but also the tooling needed around it.

You will be the first dedicated ML hire on the product taking over from the engineering manager who build the current solution and will work directly with the founding engineering team.

This is a senior, hands-on individual-contributor role, but we are small team and you'll be involved in design, planning, roadmapping, and architectural decisions.

What you will do

Design the pipelines. Own the architecture of the extraction-to-posting pipelines: page classification, field extraction, candidate retrieval, claim matching, confidence gating and the hand-off to human review, etc. Decide where rules end and models begin, and what each stage must guarantee to the next, what the separation of concerns are, etc.

We have different pipelines for different document types and expect that at any given point in time we may have new ones emerge and may consolidate others.

Evaluate new systems before we adopt them. Run structured trials of candidate components and recommend what to keep. Examples include probabilistic record linkage (Splink), Azure AI Content Understanding and Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI and Foundry-hosted models, and LLM agents with tools. Similarly, test new models with the existing pipeline as they are relased from the frontier labs.

Build the evaluation process. You'll own the process of evaluating false positives, false negatives, errors of ommission, etc, that we ultimately use to determine if we should upgrade the pipeline. 

Ship and operate. Take components from trial to production in our python workers on the cloud, instrument them, watch cost and quota, and diagnose the cases reviewers send back.

Set direction. Work with leadereship on the planing for accuracy, cost improvement, and overall product improvements.

What we are looking for

Required 

- 6+ years building ML or data-intensive systems, at least 3 of them owning a production pipeline whose output people acted on.

- Solid backend engineering understanding and ideally cloud architecture understanding.

- Ideally hands-on experience with document understanding: OCR or layout models, field extraction from scanned PDFs, or intelligent document processing products.

- Experience with entity resolution or record linkage at scale (Splink, Dedupe, Zingg, or your own blocking-and-scoring system) against databases of hundreds of thousands of rows.

- You have designed an evaluation from scratch: built a labeled ground-truth set, chosen the metrics, and defended a threshold to a non-technical stakeholder.

- Production experience with LLM APIs, including structured output, tool calling and cost or rate-limit management; you can say when an LLM is the wrong tool.

- Strong Python and SQL. Comfortable reading Postgres query plans and writing the raw query when the ORM gets in the way.

- Engineering/Scientist mindset: you are scientific about testing the pipeline and how results are interpeted/presented.

Nice to have 

- Azure AI services (Content Understanding, Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI, Foundry) or the AWS and GCP equivalents.

- Financial document processing: checks, remittance advices, lockbox files, payment matching, or accounts receivable automation.

- Exposure to collections, legal operations or other regulated workflows handling PII.

- Probabilistic matching theory (Fellegi-Sunter) or active-learning labeling workflows.

- Experience building human-review tooling or feedback loops that feed back into training and evaluation data.

How we work and what we offer

Small team, direct access to large datasets, weekly planning, daily standup, everyone remote in US timezones.

What we offer:

- A small team of tight-knit, like-minded people passionate about high quality software

- Competitive compensation, commensurate with a senior individual-contributor role.

- Monthly payments in USD

title: Engineering Lead
description:
About Doit 

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe. 

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society. 

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia. 

The Role 

Doit builds technology products used by millions of users across Southeast Asia. As our products and systems scale, we need technical leaders who can solve difficult engineering problems and raise the engineering bar around them.

The Engineering Lead owns technical direction and execution for major products and systems . This is a hands-on role - you will design systems, write code, and drive critical engineering work from idea to production.

What You'll Own 

- Owning technical design and execution for major products, systems and engineering initiatives.

- Designing scalable, reliable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

- Building alongside the team through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

- Driving architecture decisions and trade-offs across speed, scalability, reliability, cost and maintainability.

- Turning ambiguous product problems into clear technical solutions and execution plans.

- Raising engineering quality through stronger system design, testing, security, observability and development practices.

- Leading technically critical initiatives and mentoring engineers across teams.

What We're Looking For 

- 7+ years of software engineering experience building and shipping production systems.

- Deep expertise in backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

- Strong system design and architecture skills for complex or high-scale systems.

- Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

- Track record of technically leading major engineering projects from design through production.

- Ability to make sound technical trade-offs, influence engineers and solve complex production problems.

Nice to have 

- Experience scaling engineering teams, systems or development practices through significant growth.

- Experience operating across multiple products, markets or countries.

Location 

This is a remote role . We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones. 

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language 

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process 

Our process is designed to move fast:

- Online assessment or practical task

- Technical interview

- CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, LLM Inference Optimization
description:
About Nebius: 

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer on the Applied AI team at Nebius Token Factory, you will own model and endpoint optimization from model artifacts through production deployment. Your work will span model internals, quantization and model compression, speculative decoding, KV-cache optimization, inference engines, serving architecture, and benchmarking to improve latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, and cost per token while preserving quality and reliability.

You will work with kernel and platform engineers to investigate serving problems, compare configurations, and resolve performance and quality regressions. You will evaluate model- and engine-level optimizations together with distributed inference designs, including request routing, scheduling, prefill/decode coordination, and multi-node GPU execution. Your improvements will be validated through reproducible benchmarks and safe production rollouts under real-world workloads.

Your responsibilities

- Own optimization projects for specific model families, customer endpoints, or serving backends.

- Compare inference engines and recommend serving configurations suited to individual workloads.

- Diagnose model-quality and performance regressions during production rollouts.

- Improve LLM and VLM endpoint latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, quality, and cost per token.

- Deploy, configure, benchmark, and extend engines such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, and NVIDIA Dynamo.

- Develop production model-compression workflows covering quantization, quantization-aware training, distillation, low-bit serving, and accuracy recovery.

- Implement or integrate speculative decoding, draft-model approaches, KV-cache optimization, prefix caching, chunked prefill, continuous batching, and disaggregated prefill/decode serving. For prefill–decode disaggregation (PDD), evaluate KV-cache transfer, worker placement, and capacity balancing to determine which workloads benefit from the architecture.

- Design and improve LLM request routers and scheduling policies that balance worker utilization, queueing, request characteristics, and KV-cache locality while meeting latency and reliability targets.

- Scale dense and mixture-of-experts inference across multiple GPU nodes. Select and tune tensor, pipeline, data, and expert parallelism—including wide expert parallelism (WideEP)—with attention to hardware topology, expert load balance, and communication overhead.

- Build reproducible benchmark harnesses measuring TTFT, TPOT, tokens per second per GPU, p95/p99 latency, GPU memory, reliability, and cost per token. Validate architecture choices under representative traffic and consistent GPU budgets.

- Collaborate with GPU kernel and platform engineers to trace bottlenecks across model code, kernels, runtime, scheduler, gateway, and cluster layers.

- Produce design documents, performance reports, rollout plans, and customer-facing technical explanations.

Must-haves

- Strong engineering skills in Python and PyTorch.

- Hands-on experience deploying or optimizing LLM, VLM, or high-throughput transformer inference.

- Practical knowledge of at least one modern inference stack, such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, NVIDIA Dynamo, Ray Serve, KServe, or an equivalent internal system.

- A strong understanding of transformer inference bottlenecks involving KV cache, attention, memory bandwidth, batching, parallelism, and long-context serving.

- Ability to quantify trade-offs among latency, throughput, quality, utilization, and cost.

- Experience designing or optimizing distributed inference system architecture, with hands-on work in one or more areas such as request routing, distributed scheduling, PDD, multi-node inference, or expert parallelism.

- Strong communication and collaboration skills across research, kernel, infrastructure, product, and customer teams.

Nice-to-haves

- Experience with quantization-aware training, post-training quantization, FP8, INT8, INT4, NVFP4, MXFP4, AWQ, GPTQ, or SmoothQuant.

- Experience with distillation, speculative decoding, EAGLE, Medusa, multi-token prediction, or related inference acceleration methods.

- Experience supporting agentic workloads involving tool calling, structured outputs, streaming APIs, high concurrency, and multi-step orchestration.

- Familiarity with CUDA or Triton; the role does not require kernel engineering to be the candidate’s primary specialization.

- Contributions to open-source projects such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, FlashInfer, LMCache, PyTorch, Triton, Ray, or KServe.

- Implementation experience with cache-aware request routing, PDD, or WideEP, including diagnosing communication bottlenecks and load imbalance.

- Familiarity with GPU communication libraries and interconnects, such as NCCL, NVLink, InfiniBand, or RoCE.

title: Senior Product Designer (UX/UI)
description:

As Senior Product Designer you shape how our customers and operators experience Optics11’s end-to-end underwater security solutions: from in-field sensor data acquisition, through data processing, to the software platform where that data is exposed and acted on. You are part of the Product team in Underwater Security and work closely with Product Management, R&D, Engineering, Data Science, Software, Sales, Projects and Application Engineering.

No two weeks will look the same. You might join an Application Engineer in the field, interview operators and technicians, trace how sensor data flows from the field to the operator’s screen, prototype a new workflow in Figma, or review a front-end implementation with the developers. You own the user experience of our software platform, from research insight to interface design, and make sure real user needs guide decisions across technical, product and commercial teams.

Within your first 6–12 months, you will establish a shared, evidence-based view of our users through personas, journey maps and a structured insight repository; evolve our design system and UI guidelines for the software platform; and deliver interface designs for priority platform features that our developers can build with confidence. This reduces development risk and helps us deliver technology customers can trust in demanding, high-stakes environments

Responsibilities 

- Lead user and customer research: plan and run qualitative, quantitative and field studies across installation, operation and maintenance (for example alongside our Application Engineers), and translate findings into product and design decisions.

- Design the user experience of our software platform: turn product requirements from Product Management and the Product Owner into information architecture, user flows and interaction patterns for complex, data-rich operator workflows (detect, assess, identify and classify), from early concepts to interactive prototypes.

- Propose and hand over UI designs to front-end developers: create high-fidelity, build-ready designs and specifications, align on feasibility with developers and the Product Owner, and review implementations for quality and consistency.

- Own end-to-end customer journeys: map the experience from in-field deployment and data acquisition through data processing to the software platform, including demo flows and supporting internal processes.

- Manage personas and customer insights: maintain the persona set and a central research repository, and synthesise learnings collected across the organisation.

- Validate and measure outcomes: run usability tests before and after release, define adoption and usability metrics, and report impact to stakeholders.

- Evolve and maintain our design system: extend the existing basis with UI components, patterns and guidelines that keep the platform consistent, accessible and efficient to develop.

- Partner across the organisation: work closely with Product Management, Product Ownership and System Architecture, as well as Sales, Business Development, Application Engineering, Support and Marketing, to prioritise development, reduce product risk and advance user-centred practices.

Requirements 

- Master’s degree in interaction design, human-computer interaction, computer science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

- 5+ years of experience in UX or product design, covering both user research and hands-on UX/UI design, preferably in defense or other technical, high-stakes industries.

- A portfolio showing end-to-end work, from research and workflows to high-fidelity UX/UI for data-rich professional software (e.g. situational-awareness, control-room or analytics applications).

- Experience working on integrated software platforms rather than isolated websites or prototypes.

- Experience handing designs over to front-end developers and working with and evolving a design system, with a working understanding of front-end technology and its constraints.

- Proficiency in qualitative and quantitative research methods, with the ability to translate data into actionable insights and design proposals.

- Understanding of end-to-end systems in which sensor data is acquired in the field, processed and exposed on a software platform, ideally in complex or regulated environments.

- Able to translate complex technical workflows and data into clear, intuitive interfaces, with strong attention to visual detail, consistency and quality.

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English; able to present research and designs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- Proficiency in Figma and in research and collaboration tools such as Jira Product Discovery, Dovetail and Miro.

- Willingness to travel and do field research.

- Driver’s license B (or international equivalent).

- Ability to pass a background / security screening by the Dutch AIVD/MIVD, as you will be working with clients in the defense industry.

Nice to Have 

- Big plus: Experience with underwater acoustics or sonar software.

- Plus: Experience in design leadership, or in setting up design practices in a growing organisation.

- Plus: Front-end skills (e.g. HTML/CSS, React) for prototyping next to AI based tooling.

- Plus: Proficiency in Dutch.

Screening 

You will work with clients in the defense and security sectors. Obtaining a Certificate of No Objection issued by the AIVD, the Dutch General Intelligence and Security Service, is mandatory.
